x: The next two men home were Miles and Manley, also of Thames Valley, and so they scored a hollow victory in the team race. We were pleased to hear that we had been awarded second place after a tie with Portsmouth A.C., our third scoring man being placed nearer than theirs.

The next promotion in 1897, organised by Polytechnic Harriers, had at least two Belgrave competitors, Miles, who was sixth, and Poole, 7th, and the third open race over this course was held in 1903 when the now defunct Hairdressers’ A.C. were the promoting body.

Mark Miles looked in fine fettle and sure enough, as the leaders broke away from the field, he was tucked in nicely behind Herne Hill's Dave Taylor with our own Geremew Wolde, Yitbarak Dinku and Paul Freary in close attendance.

When next in view at the 2 miles point it was the home club's Stuart Major making the pace but right behind him was Taylor, and then our own Geremew Wolde and Yitbarek Dinku with Mark Miles tracking all four and looking oh! so comfortable.
But no, it wasn’t Miles, Anderson & Co. venting their frustration at being pipped by Salford Harriers – it was the world famous Horwich RMI Clog Dancers.

In Biblical terms it has been seven years of harvest since the fine six-stage squad from 1999 also placed fourth. (They were Freary, Hurst, Lobo, Evans, Miles and Barden). Paul Freary spoke to the media at length after that race.
